title: Quadratic Gaussian integral
statement:
Let $Z$ be a standard Gaussian random variable, $Z \sim N(0,1)$, and let $s \in \bbr$ satisfy $2s < 1$. Then
\[
  \E\!\left[e^{s Z^2}\right]
  = \int_{\bbr} e^{s z^2}\, \mathrm{d}N(0,1)(z)
  = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 2s}}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: integration against the standard Gaussian measure N(0,1)
replaced:
For $Z\sim N(0,1)$ and $2s<1$,
\[
  \int z.\, e^{s z^2}\,\mathrm{d}(N(0,1))
  \;=\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-2s}}.
\]
This is the closed-form moment-generating function of the standard chi-squared
distribution.
